concern: The inheritance column of gene_phenotype_seed.csv: one wrong blank, one value confirmed
why_this_is_load_bearing: `inheritance` is not decoration. `_lookup_gene_phenotype` (backend/annotation/engine.py) prefers the first association carrying HPO terms OR an inheritance pattern when choosing a gene's primary disease, and ships the value to the frontend as `inheritance_pattern`. A blank on a Mendelian row both demotes that row in primary selection and renders a monogenic disease with no inheritance mode.

C1.statement: IL10-related early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (IL10/IL10R deficiency) is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner — homozygous or compound-heterozygous loss-of-function variants in IL10, IL10RA or IL10RB.
C1.drives: Setting the IL10 row's inheritance from blank to 'Autosomal recessive'.
C1.independence: Disjoint author lists, 8 years apart, different continents and cohorts: Glocker 2009 is two unrelated European consanguineous families plus six additional early-onset colitis patients; Huang 2017 is a 42-patient Chinese VEO-IBD multicentre survey. Neither derives from the other's data.

C2.statement: VKORC1 coumarin (warfarin) resistance is autosomal dominant — heterozygous missense variants suffice. It is distinct from VKCFD2, a recessive phenotype of the same gene caused by homozygous loss of function.
C2.drives: Confirming, not changing, the VKORC1 row's existing 'Autosomal dominant'. #2043 asked for this explicitly because the row was the last survivor of #1959's AD-vs-AR observation.
C2.independence: Disjoint authors, 12 years apart. Rost 2004 is the original mapping of VKORC1 in warfarin-resistant kindreds and VKCFD2 families; Lewis 2016 is an independent clinical case with molecular-mechanism characterisation.
C2.note: The two-phenotype split is the reason this row needed confirming rather than pattern-matching off the gene symbol: the same gene is dominant for one phenotype and recessive for the other, so only the disease_name settles it.
